arguments.brief: A one-work exhibition for an art viewer inspecting the two upper-left inscriptions of Hokusai's Great Wave. Open on the entire print and title with a single button; switch to a readable portrait close-up, concise explanations and a locator thumbnail. Deep ink blue outside the print, responsive phone and laptop, no navigation or promotion.

calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout and misplaced focus after an invalid number

primary_action.observed: The full print was replaced by an enlarged detail, two explanations and a locator. The button changed to Return to the print and retained visible focus.

A-1440.edge_observation: Enter returned to the full print; visible focus remained on Read the inscriptions.
A-1440.fact_check: The visible credit identifies The Metropolitan Museum of Art, JP2569, Howard Mansfield Collection, Purchase, Rogers Fund, 1936, and says the image is public domain. The inscription interpretations and credit were not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: The full print is prominent, while the detail view shows both readable explanations alongside an enlarged crop and a locator.
A-1440.weakness: The explanations rely on spatial wording alone; the reader must look back and infer which mark corresponds to each entry.
A-1440.repair: Add restrained matching markers or leader lines to the two marks and their explanations.

primary_action.observed: Both labels, explanations and the locator appeared without scrolling. The crop and text remained side by side, with visible focus on Return to the print.

A-390.edge_observation: Enter restored the print and retained a visible focus outline on Read the inscriptions.
A-390.fact_check: The Met credit is visible in the print state. Its accuracy and the inscription interpretations were not independently verified.
A-390.strength: The entire reading task fits in the initial viewport, and the crop remains adjacent to the text.
A-390.weakness: The narrow text column and small locator make matching the explanations to marks slower; the print state also has a large empty gap above the artwork.
A-390.repair: Use direct markers for the two inscriptions and reduce the print state's vertical spacing on narrow screens.

primary_action.observed: The detail, both explanations and locator appeared in the same viewport; the button changed to Return to the print and retained visible focus.

B-1440.edge_observation: Enter restored the print with a visible focus ring on Read the inscriptions.
B-1440.fact_check: The visible credit identifies The Metropolitan Museum of Art, JP2569, Howard Mansfield Collection, Purchase, Rogers Fund, 1936, and says public domain. The inscription interpretations and credit were not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: The large crop makes both original marks prominent, and the locator clearly outlines their position in the complete print.
B-1440.weakness: A wide gap separates the crop from the explanations, slowing the visual connection between text and marks.
B-1440.repair: Bring the explanation column closer to the crop and add subtle matching identifiers to each mark.

primary_action.observed: The crop, both readable labels and explanations, locator and credit appeared without scrolling. Focus remained visibly on Return to the print.

B-390.edge_observation: Enter restored the print and left a visible focus ring on Read the inscriptions.
B-390.fact_check: The Met credit is visible in both captured states. Its accuracy and the inscription interpretations were not independently verified.
B-390.strength: The compact layout keeps the artwork, explanations and useful outlined locator together in one viewport.
B-390.weakness: The text still requires the reader to infer which mark is being discussed, and the narrow header wraps the date awkwardly in the print state.
B-390.repair: Add matching identifiers to the crop and labels, and give the artist and date enough width to avoid splitting the date.

preference.reason: A's desktop reading view places the explanations closer to the enlarged marks and gives them clearer separation. B is more compact on mobile and has a larger locator, but its desktop gap makes the central comparison less immediate. Both work by keyboard in the tested visits.
